title: Walton-on-the-Naze VII Memorial
crew_summary: 8 killed including Flt Lt. John George Clothier

external_narratives.summary: Imperial War Museums register entry for the memorial to the crew of Halifax Bomber RG475, 432 Squadron RCAF, at Walton-on-the-Naze. The crew were lost on the night of 5/6 March 1945 returning from an operational mission.
external_narratives.key_details: Crew: S/L Edwin Alfred Hayes (pilot), Flt Lt John George Clothier, P/O Douglas Marvin Cooke, F/O Colin Maxwell Hay, P/O D. Ringrose, Flt Lt Glenn Royal Harris, P/O Marius Bendt Nielsen, P/O Gilbert Melbourne Orser. Seven buried at Brookwood Cemetery, Surrey; one at Monmouth.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore detailed records of the Halifax Bomber crew's memorial at Walton-on-the-Naze VII Memorial.

external_narratives.summary: Registry entry for the Halifax RG475 memorial monument at Walton-on-the-Naze. Documents the 432 (Leaside) Squadron RCAF loss and the memorial erected in 1979.
external_narratives.key_details: Halifax VII designated QO-L with 8 recorded operations. Airscrew blades were recovered in 1979 by officers and cadets of the Colchester and Clacton Air Training Corps. Memorial dedicated that same year.
external_narratives.link_description: Walton-on-the-Naze VII Memorial: Explore the Halifax RG475 memorial honoring the fallen from 432 (Leaside) Squadron RCAF, unveiled in 1979.

external_narratives.summary: Official RCAF Association heritage page for 432 (Leaside) Squadron, documenting the unit's wartime history operating from East Moor as part of 6 Group (RCAF) Bomber Command.
external_narratives.key_details: 432 Squadron was part of the all-Canadian 6 Group, Bomber Command. Operated Halifax aircraft from RAF East Moor, Yorkshire. The squadron suffered significant losses in the final months of the war.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore the historical significance and wartime operations of 432 Squadron RCAF at Walton-on-the-Naze VII Memorial.

memorial_details:
Name: Handley Page Halifax RG475 and local men and women who served in the Royal Air Force
Type: Pillar / Column
Description: A rectangular concrete pillar on three-stepped base, with an RAF badge at the top, airscrew blades from a Halifax bomber on three sides and an inscribed plaque on the fourth side.
Inscription: THIS MEMORIAL WAS ERECTED IN 1979 BY THE FRINTON AND WALTON ROYAL AIR FORCES ASSOCIATION TO COMMEMORATE THE 60TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE/ FORMATION OF THE ROYAL AIR FORCE AND THE 30th OF THE BRANCH./ THE AIRSCREW BLADES WERE RECOVERED IN 1979 BY THE OFFICERS AND CADETS OF 308 SQUADRON OF COLCHESTER AND CLACTON AIR TRANING CORPS FROM THE SITE WHERE A/ HALIFAX BOMBER OF 432 SQUADRON, ROYAL CANADIAN AIR FORCE, CRASHED AT THE NAZE ON THE NIGHT OF MARCH 5/6 1945 WHILST RETURNING FROM AN OPERATIONAL/ MISSION, KILLING ALL MEMBERS OF THE CREW./ THE MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO ALL LOCAL MEN AND WOMEN WHO HAVE SERVED IN THE ROYAL AIR FORCE AND TO THE MEMORY OF THE HALIFAX CREW/ (Names)/ SEVEN OF THE ABOVE ARE BURIED AT BROOKWOOD, SURREY AND ONE AT MONMOUTH, S WALES
Location: Garden of Remembrance Corner of High Street and Church Road Walton On The Naze Tendring Essex CO14 8BN England
Grid Ref: TM 25163 21681
Coordinates: 51.848286369510,1.267736191972
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/86/477/large_raf_mem_.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/86/494/large_raf_mem_1.jpg

This memorial was erected in that same year to honor the 60th anniversary of the Royal Air Force's formation and the 30th of its local branch, dedicated to all who served and to the memory of the ill-fated Halifax crew.

The memorial is a rectangular concrete pillar on a three-stepped base, with a RAF badge at the top and an inscribed plaque on the base.

Memorial Dedication: Dedication of the Handley Page Halifax RG475 and local men and women who served in the Royal Air Force memorial.

The text describes a memorial dedicated to Handley Page Halifax RG475 and local men and women who served in the Royal Air Force. The memorial was created by Mike Peck (WMR-22943).
narrative: In 1945, on March 6th, a Halifax VII RG475 of 432 Squadron, Royal Canadian Air Force, tragically crashed at The Naze during its return from an operational mission. This occurred as part of World War II. All crew members perished in the incident. In 1979, airscrew blades were recovered by officers and cadets of 308 Squadron from this site. Seven of these crew members are interred at Brookwood, Surrey, while one lies in Monmouth, South Wales.
